samples.summary: Cleanup sweeps are a second store write, so they are a second undo unit under the Yorkie store — contradicting the stated "one undo unit" design property
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op and undo units are per `doc.update()` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2733`: "Yorkie tracks undo units via doc.update() — no-op"). `Doc.setBlockType` issues `store.setBlockType(...)` and then a separate `store.applyStyles(...)` via `dropStaleStyleOff`; `afterNamedStyleChange` (`view/editor.ts:1052`) likewise runs `docStore.updateStyleDefinition/...` and then `dropStaleStyleOffAll` → `applyStyles`; the paste path does `insertBlocks(...)` then `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (`view/text-editor.ts:1258-1264`). Each is a distinct `doc.update()`, so Cmd+Z first undoes only the cleanup, leaving the block type / style redefinition / paste in place with the flags restored. Both the code comments ("batches its writes, so the redefinition and the cleanup undo as one step", editor.ts:1049-1050) and the design doc ("Both sweeps write through `DocStore.applyStyles`, so a redefinition stays one undo unit however many runs it strands", docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md) assert a property the implementation only gives for the *runs inside* one sweep, not for the operation plus its sweep. `applyStyles` batching solves intra-sweep granularity but not the operation+sweep pairing.

samples.summary: The "one merge rule" consolidation is incomplete: two more copies of the adjacent-inline merge remain, one of them still lacking the structural-inline exception the change was made for
samples.evidence: The diff folds `Doc.mergeCells`'s private copy into `normalizeInlines` on the explicit rationale that "a second copy here drifted from it and re-merged structural inlines". But `clipboard.ts:mergeInlines` (line 445) still merges any pair whose `inlineStylesEqual` agrees, with no `isStructuralInline` guard and no empty-run skip — the same drift, on the HTML-paste path that can carry two identical images. `TextEditor.normalizeInlineList` (`view/text-editor.ts:3816`) is a third copy, with its own hand-rolled equality `inlineStylesMatch` (3836) that compares a subset of keys — so clearing a key (the whole point of #749) can now make runs equal under one comparator and not the other. block-helpers.ts:87 even names that copy as the reference rule rather than reusing it.

samples.summary: Architecture change to the named-style redefinition path is not recorded in docs-named-styles.md and brushes against its stated Non-Goal
samples.evidence: `setDocStyles` / `updateStyleToMatch` / `resetNamedStyle` / `resetAllNamedStyles` now rewrite *run styles* across body, header, footer and every nested table cell (`Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll`), which changes the named-styles subsystem contract: a redefinition used to be a registry-only write with lazy inline resolution (docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md:121 "Inline … lazy, registry-driven"). That doc is untouched; the whole invariant lives in docs-font-controls.md, a toolbar-UI doc, with no cross-link. docs-named-styles.md:42-43 also lists as a Non-Goal "Character-level cascade for *direct* formatting tracking … beyond what already exists", and a document-wide sweep that rewrites direct run formatting when a style is redefined is exactly that kind of character-level tracking.

samples.summary: Design doc's "out of scope: legacy `false` flags are left alone" contradicts what the sweeps actually do
samples.evidence: The new section ends with "Out of scope: `false` flags already stored by older builds are left alone — they resolve identically and are cleared the next time the user toggles that key." But `Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll` walks every block in the document (body/header/footer/all nested cells) and clears every stale boolean `false` it finds, and it is invoked on any named-style change *and* on every internal-clipboard paste (`view/text-editor.ts:1264`). So legacy flags on blocks the user never touched are rewritten — a CRDT write burst on unrelated runs (and, collaboratively, remote content churn) that the spec text says will not happen. Either the sweep should be scoped to the affected blocks or the doc's out-of-scope claim is wrong.

samples.summary: Unrequested behavioral changes bundled into the Yorkie `applyStyle` write path, beyond the issue's scope
samples.evidence: Two changes here are not required by #749's scope (which is: demote boolean `false` in `Doc`, drop `undefined` keys in block-helpers, tests): (a) the tree write no longer re-asserts the node's existing attributes, changing concurrent-edit semantics for *all* inline keys including non-boolean ones — the task's Non-goals explicitly exclude "Any non-boolean style key" (docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:66); (b) `resolveScriptExclusion` is applied to the tree write, fixing a pre-existing CRDT/cache divergence for superscript/subscript that is an independent bug with its own test. Both may be desirable, but they widen the blast radius of a hot-path change without an issue backing them.

samples.summary: Model layer hard-codes a view-layer default (renderRun's link underline), with no shared helper to prevent drift
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear`/`collectStaleStyleOff` in `model/document.ts` encode the rule "an `href` run with absent `underline` renders underlined", which is owned by `view/paint-layout.ts:renderRun`. The two sites are kept in sync only by comments pointing at each other (paint-layout.ts:385-389). A shared predicate (e.g. `linkImpliesUnderline(style)` next to the renderer's default) would keep the defaulting layer in one place; as written, changing the link default in the view silently makes the model's exception wrong.

samples.summary: Paste uses the whole-document sweep where only the pasted blocks can be stale
samples.evidence: `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` re-reads the store, walks body + header + footer + every nested table cell, and can emit an `applyStyles` batch spanning blocks unrelated to the paste. The pasted blocks are known at this call site (`data.blocks` / `insertBlocks`), so a block-scoped sweep (the `collectStaleStyleOff([...])` primitive already exists, and `dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)` is its single-block form) would be the matching granularity and avoid touching untouched content.

samples.summary: Engine-wide storage invariant documented inside a toolbar/UI-scoped design doc
samples.evidence: The new "Storage invariant: a boolean turned off is *cleared*" section spans `Doc`, `store/block-helpers`, `normalizeInlines`, the Yorkie CRDT write path, the format painter and the paste path — none of which are font controls. Its home is docs-font-controls.md only because the earlier `''`-clear normalization (#728/#793) landed there. Folding into the canonical engine doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md) or docs-named-styles.md, with a pointer from here, would match the repo's "one canonical subsystem doc" filing; at minimum the named-styles and pending-inline-style docs should cross-link, since both layers now participate in the rule.

samples.summary: The link exception deliberately re-introduces the dead flags the change exists to remove, at slice granularity
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` keeps `underline: false` for the entire slice whenever any run in it carries an `href`, so plain runs beside a link get exactly the un-mergeable dead flag #749 is about. The tradeoff is documented and defensible, but a per-run decision (which `collectStaleStyleOff` already does when sweeping) would satisfy the invariant without the compromise, and would make the model's two code paths agree on granularity.

finding.summary: Cleanup sweeps are a second store write, so they are a second undo unit under the Yorkie store — contradicting the stated "one undo unit" design property
finding.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op and undo units are per `doc.update()` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2733`: "Yorkie tracks undo units via doc.update() — no-op"). `Doc.setBlockType` issues `store.setBlockType(...)` and then a separate `store.applyStyles(...)` via `dropStaleStyleOff`; `afterNamedStyleChange` (`view/editor.ts:1052`) likewise runs `docStore.updateStyleDefinition/...` and then `dropStaleStyleOffAll` → `applyStyles`; the paste path does `insertBlocks(...)` then `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (`view/text-editor.ts:1258-1264`). Each is a distinct `doc.update()`, so Cmd+Z first undoes only the cleanup, leaving the block type / style redefinition / paste in place with the flags restored. Both the code comments ("batches its writes, so the redefinition and the cleanup undo as one step", editor.ts:1049-1050) and the design doc ("Both sweeps write through `DocStore.applyStyles`, so a redefinition stays one undo unit however many runs it strands", docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md) assert a property the implementation only gives for the *runs inside* one sweep, not for the operation plus its sweep. `applyStyles` batching solves intra-sweep granularity but not the operation+sweep pairing.

verdict.reason: All presence claims check out. YorkieDocStore.snapshot() is a no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) and undo granularity is per doc.update() — the DocStore contract says so explicitly (store.ts:82-89). Doc.setBlockType writes store.setBlockType (doc.update at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1461) and then a separate store.applyStyles (doc.update at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806) via dropStaleStyleOff (document.ts:606-611, 562-568). afterNamedStyleChange (editor.ts:1052-1056) similarly runs dropStaleStyleOffAll after the caller's own store write (e.g. setDocStyles' doc.update at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710), and the internal-paste branch does insertBlocks then dropStaleStyleOffAll (text-editor.ts:1256-1264). The editor's undo pops exactly one unit (editor.ts:1995-1998), and I found no transaction/grouping mechanism in YorkieDocStore that would fuse consecutive doc.update() calls. Meanwhile editor.ts:1049-1050 and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:355-356 assert the operation+sweep undo as one step — a property applyStyles batching only delivers for runs *within* a sweep. This is a real design-doc/implementation mismatch (documented design property not delivered), so I cannot refute it on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds.

finding.summary: The "one merge rule" consolidation is incomplete: two more copies of the adjacent-inline merge remain, one of them still lacking the structural-inline exception the change was made for
finding.evidence: The diff folds `Doc.mergeCells`'s private copy into `normalizeInlines` on the explicit rationale that "a second copy here drifted from it and re-merged structural inlines". But `clipboard.ts:mergeInlines` (line 445) still merges any pair whose `inlineStylesEqual` agrees, with no `isStructuralInline` guard and no empty-run skip — the same drift, on the HTML-paste path that can carry two identical images. `TextEditor.normalizeInlineList` (`view/text-editor.ts:3816`) is a third copy, with its own hand-rolled equality `inlineStylesMatch` (3836) that compares a subset of keys — so clearing a key (the whole point of #749) can now make runs equal under one comparator and not the other. block-helpers.ts:87 even names that copy as the reference rule rather than reusing it.

verdict.reason: The presence claim holds. `normalizeInlines` (store/block-helpers.ts:89-112) is the canonical rule with the structural guard (96-97) and empty-run skip (92), and document.ts:957-963 folds one copy into it on exactly the quoted rationale. But clipboard.ts:445-455 is a second copy that merges purely on `inlineStylesEqual` with no `isStructuralInline` guard and no empty-text skip, and text-editor.ts:3816-3854 is a third copy with its own `inlineStylesMatch` (3836) that omits `pageNumber`/`image` and compares StoredColor by `===` where `inlineStylesEqual` uses `storedColorsEqual` (model/types.ts:485-497). block-helpers.ts:86-87 literally names the TextEditor copy as the peer "same rule" reference instead of having it call the shared helper. That is duplication of an existing shared module in a repo that expects reuse — `major` kind under this lens. Caveats that lower my confidence but do not supply a refutation ground: clipboard.ts has no `` handling at all (zero `img` matches; `sanitizeImageData`:110 serves the JSON WAFFLEDOCS path via `sanitizeInlines`:166, not `mergeInlines`), so the specific "two identical images on the HTML-paste path" harm is not reachable there today; and the #749 comparator argument is wrong in detail (both comparators treat cleared keys identically as `undefined`). Those weaken the stated consequences, not the existence of the two unconsolidated copies, so the finding stays.

finding.summary: Architecture change to the named-style redefinition path is not recorded in docs-named-styles.md and brushes against its stated Non-Goal
finding.evidence: `setDocStyles` / `updateStyleToMatch` / `resetNamedStyle` / `resetAllNamedStyles` now rewrite *run styles* across body, header, footer and every nested table cell (`Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll`), which changes the named-styles subsystem contract: a redefinition used to be a registry-only write with lazy inline resolution (docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md:121 "Inline … lazy, registry-driven"). That doc is untouched; the whole invariant lives in docs-font-controls.md, a toolbar-UI doc, with no cross-link. docs-named-styles.md:42-43 also lists as a Non-Goal "Character-level cascade for *direct* formatting tracking … beyond what already exists", and a document-wide sweep that rewrites direct run formatting when a style is redefined is exactly that kind of character-level tracking.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is that the named-style redefinition sweep is not recorded in a design doc. It is: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:337-358 documents the whole invariant explicitly — "Every such entry point (setDocStyles, updateStyleToMatch, resetNamedStyle, resetAllNamedStyles) runs Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll over the whole document — body, header, footer, and every nested table cell — via afterNamedStyleChange", plus the single-undo-unit batching contract, matching packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1039-1059 and packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:480-518. That doc is linked in docs/design/README.md:53 and is not a parallel file: the section is the canonical home of the issue-#749 run-style clear semantics (docs-font-controls.md:313-408), sitting beside the sibling '' color-clear model-layer contract at :280-311, and inline-clear behavior is one of the doc's stated Goals (:40-42) — so the "fold into the canonical subsystem doc" discipline is met. The Non-Goal cited (docs-named-styles.md:42-43, character-level cascade for direct formatting tracking) is not exceeded: dropStaleStyleOffAll (document.ts:499-524) only deletes boolean false keys whose named-style under-layer stopped supplying them, the same cleanup that already existed for block-type changes (document.ts:474-478, called at :611), and the originating task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:22-27) names this lazy-cascade hazard as the problem being fixed. The only residue is the lack of a cross-link from docs-named-styles.md, which is a cross-reference preference (minor) and never blocks.

finding.summary: Design doc's "out of scope: legacy `false` flags are left alone" contradicts what the sweeps actually do
finding.evidence: The new section ends with "Out of scope: `false` flags already stored by older builds are left alone — they resolve identically and are cleared the next time the user toggles that key." But `Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll` walks every block in the document (body/header/footer/all nested cells) and clears every stale boolean `false` it finds, and it is invoked on any named-style change *and* on every internal-clipboard paste (`view/text-editor.ts:1264`). So legacy flags on blocks the user never touched are rewritten — a CRDT write burst on unrelated runs (and, collaboratively, remote content churn) that the spec text says will not happen. Either the sweep should be scoped to the affected blocks or the doc's out-of-scope claim is wrong.

verdict.reason: The quoted doc sentence and the document-wide sweep both exist as described (docs-font-controls.md:405-408; document.ts:499-518 walking body/header/footer/nested cells; callers at editor.ts:1052-1060 and text-editor.ts:1255-1268). But the finding's premise that "the spec text says this will not happen" is not supported: the same section explicitly documents the whole-document scope — line 346-349 says every named-style entry point runs `dropStaleStyleOffAll` "over the whole document — body, header, footer, and every nested table cell", line 350-353 documents the internal-paste sweep, and line 354-355 documents the batched single-undo write. The trailing "Out of scope" prose is an inline note about not adding a dedicated legacy-document migration pass (mirroring the identical note at 308-311 for `''` values), and no such migration exists (no load-time migration in packages/docs/src). The doc's normative scope statement is the "Non-Goals (as originally scoped)" section at line 48, which this note is not part of, so no stated Non-Goal is exceeded, no design doc is missing or parallel, no module is duplicated, and no acceptance criterion is shown unmet. The proposed alternative remedy (scope the sweep to "affected blocks") is incoherent for the named-style path, since redefining a style is precisely what strands flags on runs the user never touched (document.ts:480-498). What is left is a single loosely-worded sentence that reads more absolutely than the behaviour documented six paragraphs above it — documentation polish, i.e. minor under this lens's severity rubric ("preferences, taste, could be cleaner"), which never blocks.

finding.summary: Unrequested behavioral changes bundled into the Yorkie `applyStyle` write path, beyond the issue's scope
finding.evidence: Two changes here are not required by #749's scope (which is: demote boolean `false` in `Doc`, drop `undefined` keys in block-helpers, tests): (a) the tree write no longer re-asserts the node's existing attributes, changing concurrent-edit semantics for *all* inline keys including non-boolean ones — the task's Non-goals explicitly exclude "Any non-boolean style key" (docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:66); (b) `resolveScriptExclusion` is applied to the tree write, fixing a pre-existing CRDT/cache divergence for superscript/subscript that is an independent bug with its own test. Both may be desirable, but they widen the blast radius of a hot-path change without an issue backing them.

verdict.reason: Both cited behaviors exist in the working tree exactly as described. yorkie-doc-store.ts:1951-1961 sends only the patch's own attributes (styleByPath + removeStyleByPath) and the adjacent comment at 1946-1950 explicitly frames this as *not* re-asserting the node's existing attributes, a concurrent-edit semantics decision that applies to every inline key, not just booleans. Line 1951 also applies resolveScriptExclusion to the tree write; block-helpers.ts:401-420 shows the helper was extracted and exported specifically so the Yorkie store could reuse it, and yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:230-245 adds a dedicated test for a divergence the test comment itself describes as pre-existing (tree kept both script flags while the cache dropped one). Neither behavior appears in the task's Scope list (todo.md:49-58), which covers only the Doc-level boolean demotion, the block-helpers undefined-key drop, and tests. No refutation ground fits: the code is present as described, it is on the live applyStyle/applyStyles path (lines 1769, 1813) so it is reachable, and scope creep versus the issue's Scope/Non-goals is within the design-fit lens. My confidence is low only because I could not inspect the pre-change revision to confirm the tree write previously re-asserted existing attributes; per the verifier rules that "did the change introduce it" question is decided separately, and uncertainty keeps the finding.
